Electromagnetic design report · FEMM 4.2 · 2D magnetostatic

v7 Motor EM Report

12-slot / 10-pole spoke-ferrite PMSM for an EV two-wheeler, 52 V battery, delta winding. Model calibrated to the Motor-CAD peak torque of 45 N·m. All figures below come from the FEMM solutions in femm_em/.

key results, calibrated model
Peak torque @ 360 A rms45.0N·mcurrent angle 23.2°
Base speed (11 kW DC limit)2200rpm3300 rpm without the DC limit
Max shaft power10.5kWheld to 12 000 rpm (battery-limited)
Peak motor efficiency97.0%at 5250 rpm, 16 N·m
Back-EMF, line-line7.80V rms/krpmψm 0.0211 Wb-turn per path
Magnet demag at rated-664kA/mHcJ −340; 0.2 % of magnet area past HcJ
  • The motor makes 45.0 N·m at 360 A rms with a torque ripple of 5.0 % and cogging of only 0.075 N·m peak-to-peak.
  • On the 52 V battery the 11 kW DC limit, not the motor, sets the speed range: full torque to about 2200 rpm, then about 10.5 kW at the shaft up to 12 000 rpm.
  • Saliency Lq/Ld ≈ 1.22 gives useful reluctance torque, so the best current angle is 23.2° rather than 0°.
  • Action needed: at rated current the field at the magnet tips beside the slot opening passes the ferrite HcJ (local irreversible demagnetisation). See Demagnetisation.

Efficiency and loss maps

minimum-loss current at every point inside the envelope

Iron loss is an estimate from the no-load flux distribution scaled with the operating flux and a typical M235-35A loss curve. Treat efficiency above ~6000 rpm as ±1–2 %. AC copper (proximity) loss in the Ø2.9 mm wire is not included and will lower high-speed efficiency.

Magnet demagnetisation check

H along the magnetisation direction
CaseMost negative H (kA/m)vs HcJ −340
No load-179OK
Rated, γ 23.2°-664past HcJ
Rated, pure −d (γ 90°)-495past HcJ
Magnet area past HcJ (rated)0.2 %
Magnet area past 80 % of HcJ0.8 %

Local irreversible demagnetisation is predicted at the magnet tips at rated current. Ferrite HcJ also falls in the cold (≈ −0.2 to −0.3 %/K), so a cold start at full current is the worst case. Options: a higher-HcJ ferrite grade, thicker pole-piece lips over the magnet top, a smaller magnet opening, or a lower peak current.

Limitations

what a 2D magnetostatic model leaves out
  • End-winding leakage inductance (end turns ≈ ⅓ of the wire length) is not in Ld/Lq: real base speed will be a few hundred rpm lower.
  • 3D end effects of the ferrite spoke rotor (axial leakage) typically cost 5–15 % torque. The calibration to Motor-CAD absorbs part of this only if Motor-CAD included it.
  • Iron loss is estimated, not solved per element over time; AC copper and magnet eddy losses are omitted.
  • Thermal: 360 A rms is ≈15.8 A/mm² in the wire, a short-time rating. Continuous capability needs a thermal model.
  • Mechanical: rotor bridge stress at 12 000 rpm is not checked.
